healthBenefits.title: Rich in Fiber
healthBenefits.text: Green beans provide dietary fiber that supports digestion and helps maintain healthy blood sugar levels.

healthBenefits.title: Vitamin C Boost
healthBenefits.text: Lemon juice and green beans supply vitamin C, supporting immune function and collagen production.

healthBenefits.title: Anti-inflammatory Herbs
healthBenefits.text: Mint and parsley contain antioxidants and volatile oils that may help reduce inflammation and aid digestion.

healthBenefits.title: Heart-Healthy Fats
healthBenefits.text: Extra virgin olive oil provides monounsaturated fats that support cardiovascular health.

healthBenefits.title: Onion Benefits
healthBenefits.text: Onions contain sulfur compounds and antioxidants like quercetin, which may support heart health and reduce inflammation.

healthBenefits.title: Low Calorie, Nutrient Dense
healthBenefits.text: This dish is naturally low in calories while offering vitamins, minerals, and fiber, making it a wholesome side dish.

_ingredientsText:
1 Kg of green beans
• 1 onion, chopped
• 1 tablespoon parsley, chopped
• 1 1⁄2 tablespoons bread crumbs
• 1 tablespoon chopped mint or thyme
• juice of 1 lemon
• 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil
• salt
• pepper (optional)
_preparationText:
Clean the beans and boil them in salted water for 15 minutes. As soon as they are cooked, drain and set aside.
2. In a pan, add the olive oil, fry the chopped onion, and then add the green beans. Cook for 3 minutes, adding the cooking water used to cook the beans if necessary.
3. Immediately add the breadcrumbs, mint, parsley, lemon juice, and pepper. Cook for 2 minutes.
4. Serve on individual plates adding fresh mint leaves for garnish.
